leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight round-1 files name massively parallel sequencing by synthesis (B017) in their preferred configuration, which is the only ballot ID that reaches five explicit supporters. All five describe the same scientific core: reversible-terminator, fluorescent-nucleotide chemistry on surface-clustered templates, in use for about two decades. They do not share a laureate set. Aili, Brzezinski and Chabes prefer Balasubramanian and Klenerman only; Aqvist and Linke add Pascal Mayer for clonal amplification or the clustered array concept. Citation wording also differs: Aili, Brzezinski and Chabes name reversible terminators and clusters, Aqvist and Linke use broader 'sequencing by synthesis' phrasing, and Linke's wording would need to address the pyrosequencing and semiconductor routes. Ju and Rothberg are in no member's preferred configuration. Aili and Aqvist state they would accept the other laureate count under conditions (Aili would not oppose Mayer if expert reports show the cluster idea was decisive; Aqvist names the Cambridge pair alone as the cleaner fallback).

Brzezinski proposes a two-part prize: the B017 Cambridge pair plus nitrogenase structure (B003) credited to Douglas Rees alone. He explicitly says he would not push B003 as a three-person prize against the weight of the openings, and acknowledges that a Rees-only citation leaves out Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe and that the two parts have no obvious joint motivation. No other member lists B003 as a preferred part; Chabes lists it as an alternative.

Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) as a single-part prize, arguing for the cleanest two-person attribution and for C-N bond formation as a distinct catalyst-design problem from the 2010 C-C coupling prize. B048 is a listed alternative for Aili, Aqvist and Linke. Their stated reservations are that it may be viewed as an extension of the 2010 framework and that Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work needs handling in the citation.

Sparr prefers biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as a single-part prize, valued as a new physical-chemical concept of cellular organisation. She herself identifies the main weaknesses: contested in vivo evidence, an unclear chemistry versus cell biology fit, and the exclusion of Pappu and Mittag by a three-name cut. B029 is not a preferred part for any other member; Brzezinski lists it as an alternative.

Zou prefers molecular-sieve catalyst design (Corma, Davis, Zones) as a single-part prize, citing decades of independent confirmation and three distinct contributions. Zou concedes it is a broad accumulated field rather than a single discovery, that Yu and Tsapatsis have claims, and that it is a minority view; Zou lists B017 as an alternative. No other member lists B041.

areas_of_agreement: No member argues that B017 is immature. Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Linke call it overdue or two decades confirmed, and Brzezinski says two decades of use remove any maturity question.
Balasubramanian and Klenerman are in every B017 configuration (five of five), and no member proposes a B017 prize without them.
Every B017 supporter, and several others, identify attribution beyond the Cambridge pair (Mayer, Ju, Rothberg) as the main open weakness of B017.

Several files, including those of Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Brzezinski and Somfai, name the same objection to B017: that sequencing already had a Chemistry prize in 1980 (Sanger and Gilbert) and may look like a scale-up or a biology and medicine tool.

Three of the non-B017 first choices (Zou, Somfai, Sparr) list B017 or B045 among their alternatives, and Zou and Sparr explicitly list B017 as an alternative. Brzezinski carries B017 in his own configuration. No member states opposition to B017 on scientific grounds.
All eight files report no specific conflict preventing participation; the disclosures are field proximity or institutional colleagueship.
scientific_disputes: Whether B017 is a new chemical principle or an extension of Sanger-type sequencing: Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Linke raise this, and Aili, Chabes and Linke want the citation to say clearly that the discovery is chemistry rather than medicine.
Whether B048 is a distinct catalyst-design problem (Somfai) or an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling framework (Aili, Aqvist, Somfai's own case against).
Whether the physical-chemical concept in B029 is established enough in vivo, given criticism about overexpression and crowding artefacts (Sparr, Aili).
Whether B041 is one discovery or an accumulated field (Zou's own case against).
Whether the B003 core (structure and cofactor composition, per Brzezinski) can be cleanly separated from the still debated mechanism of N2 binding.
Linke notes the weight to give perovskite stability (B045) against reproducibility of the absorber discovery; Aili treats B045 as later rather than poor.
attribution_disputes: B017: two-name (Balasubramanian, Klenerman; Aili, Brzezinski, Chabes) versus three-name with Mayer (Aqvist, Linke). The case for Mayer rests on clonal amplification or the clustered array concept; Chabes and Aqvist say priority evidence has not been verified from the material provided.

B017: Ju (terminator chemistry) and Rothberg (pyrosequencing and semiconductor sequencing) are excluded by every preferred configuration but credited as having genuine claims by Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes and Linke. Aqvist notes the 454 lineage would be left out entirely.
B003: Rees-only (Brzezinski) leaves out Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe.
B048: Kosugi's tin-amide precedent, and the relative priority of Buchwald and Hartwig on first catalytic examples (Somfai).
B029: Pappu and Mittag are excluded from a Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen cut (Sparr, Aili).
B041: Yu and Tsapatsis may displace one of Corma, Davis and Zones (Zou).
maturity_disputes: B017 is described as mature by all five of its supporters; no maturity dispute is stated for it.
B029: the status of in vivo evidence and limited technological consequence (Sparr, Aili).
B003: the catalytic mechanism is still debated (Brzezinski).
B052 (alternative for Aili, Brzezinski): the absence of an approved degrader drug is raised by Aili, and Zou asks how much weight clinical benefit should carry.
B045: long-term stability and lead content (Aili, Linke) are described as unresolved.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Zou-Xiaodong discloses close field proximity to B041, and also to B060 and B018 (electron crystallography of zeolites, MOFs and porous materials); no personal or institutional tie to Corma, Davis or Zones is reported.
Sparr-Emma flags proximity between her lipid self-assembly research and B067 (an alternative of hers); no link to the named candidates is reported.
Brzezinski-Peter discloses scientific proximity to B003 (a metalloenzyme with proton-coupled electron transfer) and Stockholm University colleagueship with Zou; neither is stated to be a conflict.
Aqvist-Johan discloses a Warshel/EVB and biomolecular simulation background related to B037 and does not support B037.
Chabes-Andrei discloses use of sequencing and mass-spectrometry nucleotide measurement in his own work, as field proximity with no tie to B017 candidates.
Aili-Daniel notes research overlap with Sparr on self-assembly as scientific proximity, not a recusal issue.
Lund colleagueship among Linke, Somfai and Sparr is disclosed by all three as not a conflict. No member reports a recusal.
questions_for_round2: For B017, should the laureate set be Balasubramanian and Klenerman alone, or should Mayer be added as a third laureate for clonal amplification or the clustered array concept? What priority and experimental evidence would settle Mayer against Ju or Rothberg?

Can a B017 citation be worded to credit sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry without appearing to exclude the pyrosequencing and semiconductor routes arbitrarily, and should it say explicitly that the recognised discovery is chemistry?

Does the committee regard B017 as a new chemical capability or as an extension of the sequencing work recognised in 1980, and do Somfai, Sparr and Zou, who did not place it first, hold an objection to B017 beyond preferring their own candidate?
If B017 proceeds, is a second prize part warranted at all, and if so which: B003 (Rees only, or a wider set), B048, B029 or B041? What would a joint motivation for two unrelated parts be?
For B048, does the C-N coupling constitute a distinct catalyst-design concept relative to the 2010 prize, and how should Kosugi's precedent be handled in the citation?

For B029, B003 and B041, what is the minimal claim that can be defended on maturity and attribution (for example, the founding observation only for B029, structure and cofactor composition only for B003, or whether B041 is one discovery)?
Do the members who did not rank B017 in their opening top eight (as Aili states for Brzezinski, Sparr, Somfai and Zou) accept it as a viable prize part, and under what laureate set?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 positions, B017 is the only ballot with majority-level support (five of eight, though with two different laureate sets), while B048, B029 and B041 each have one explicit preferred-configuration supporter and B003 appears as a preferred part only with Brzezinski. The remaining open work is attribution within B017 (two names or three, and the status of Ju and Rothberg), the wording of the citation, whether a second prize part is needed, and whether the three members who preferred other single-part prizes would accept B017. No hidden votes are inferred from these files.
